label: outputting r/l/3, or early inputs v/j/i/a (t<=2)
explanation: Two unrelated components. (1) Delimiter/copy phase: fires when the token being output is r (41% rate, 8.3x lift), l (31%) or 3 (22%), weaker for g/h/x. The strongest activations of all are at the <DEL> step when the first original token is r (about 1.0 of max). (2) Original phase, positions 0-2 (mostly t=1-2): fires when the input is v, j, i or a (15-25% rate). Original-phase activity almost disappears from position 4 onward. Each component alone has low precision (0.3-0.5), so this is a broad, token-identity-driven neuron, not a clean detector. Dev scores: F1 0.54, mass recall 0.77, precision 0.43. Missed mass (~23%) is spread over other tokens and positions. It is not modulated by copy correctness or token repetition (in_count).
